name: Extreme heat exposure
unscored_reason: No adopted or scientifically defensible safe annual number of locally extreme-temperature days was established. The 95th-percentile rule defines an exposure event; it is not a safe annual-day target. Historical climatological averages, forecast HeatRisk categories, occupational exposure limits and zero days are not adopted annual targets for this measure.
source: Derived from CDC/ATSDR Environmental Justice Index 2024: 2018–2022 extreme-heat days and ACS population
notes: MONTEREY COUNTY PROXY / CONTEXT ONLY. This is not a Carmel-by-the-Sea city observation. Coastal Carmel can differ materially from inland county heat exposure. No recent city-only observed series was established. Observation period: 2018–2022 annual average; year=2022 is the period end, not a single-year count. Derived resident-weighted county exposure summary: sum(E_NEHD × E_TOTPOP) / sum(E_TOTPOP) = 6,351,206.4 / 437,609 = 14.513427283259714 days/year. All 103 Monterey County tracts included in CDC EJI 2024; Census 2020 lists 104 county tracts, with water-only zero-population tract 06053990000 absent from EJI. The remaining 103 cover the county resident land geography. No residents are removed by this water-tract omission. This is an observed membership difference; CDC documentation does not state a removal policy. CDC EJI 2024 E_NEHD is the annual mean for 2018–2022, computed as the five-year sum divided by five. The included dictionary defines a day as maximum temperature exceeding the tract-specific historical 95th percentile; this is a relative local-temperature criterion. Weights E_TOTPOP are 2018–2022 ACS S0601 population estimates from the same package. Both fields agree across all 103 tracts between the official CSV package and CDC data service; none is missing or negative. This is a weighted mean of tract annual means, not the number of days when the entire county simultaneously exceeded a threshold, an absolute-temperature count, heat-index count, NWS HeatRisk, or future projection. CDC crosswalked heat from 2010 to 2020 tracts; nationally 13 missing tracts were interpolated but the local interpolation status is not identified. The EJI heat entry does not specify historical baseline years or seasonal window; do not import a baseline from Cal-Adapt or another CDC series. Tract annual means range 6.8–18.4. Source tier 1 searched: Carmel 2021 vulnerability assessment and 2022 adaptation plan give modeled baseline and projections (>87.9°F), not a recent observed city series; the county economic report gives 2010–2024 mean nine days >=92.5°F but its Cal-Adapt observed/projected split is insufficiently documented for acceptance. County 2026 public draft climate plan provides old historical baselines and projections. Tier 2 official retrospective CDC EJI series accepted; direct CDC Tracking county API requests were rate-limited (429), not treated as evidence of no data. Reproduction and raw hash manifest are in calculations/extreme-heat/.
